property_summary: After the owner calls NETM(), the owner's balance equals totalDistributed (the reference always sets balances[owner]==totalDistributed); the mutant omits that assignment so for some inputs the equality can be false.

After calling NETM() by the owner, the reference contract always sets the owner's balance to totalDistributed (so balances(owner) == totalDistributed); the mutant that zeroes balances[owner] breaks this by making balances(owner) == 0 for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner, invoking NETM() leaves totalDistributed unchanged and balances(owner) equal to totalDistributed (i.e., balances[owner] == totalDistributed); the mutant wrongly increases balances[owner] by 1e18 causing balances[owner] != totalDistributed for some inputs.

In the reference contract only the current owner can call NETM() which assigns totalDistributed tokens to the owner (so balances[owner] increases and no other address gains those tokens); the mutant removing the onlyOwner check allows any caller to become owner via NETM and thus can change which address receives the minted distribution, violating that balances[address] is unchanged for arbitrary addresses when NETM is invoked by a non-owner.

Calling NETM() by any caller other than the current owner must NOT increase the token balance of an unrelated target address in the reference contract (only owner can trigger NETM so balances[target] remains unchanged for arbitrary caller), whereas the mutant that removes onlyOwner can let a non-owner call NETM and become owner causing balances[target] to change for some input addresses.

In the reference contract only the original owner (deployer) can call NETM(), so calling NETM() from any arbitrary caller never increases balances[target] for a target that is not the original owner; the mutant that removes onlyOwner allows a non-owner to call NETM() and make themselves owner thereby increasing balances of some addresses (breaking the invariant).

Invariant: calling NETM() never changes the balance of the originally-deployed owner address (the deployer) for any caller; the mutant that removes onlyOwner lets an attacker become owner and assign the distributed tokens to themselves, which can change the deployer's balance for some caller inputs.

Invariant: calling NETM() by any caller never increases the balance of any address other than the contract's owner at the time of deployment (the original deployer); the mutant removing onlyOwner allows non-owners to call NETM() and become owner, causing balances for some addresses to increase that shouldn't under the reference.
